title: Ethiopian Gurage Spiced Beef
community: Gurage people of central Ethiopia — the hospitality beef tradition
author: Chef Haile
desc: Gurage Spiced Beef — beef cooked in the Gurage style that gave rise to kitfo, with mekelesha (cardamom, rue, and coriander) as the primary seasoning alongside kibbeh. Less raw than kitfo, more fully cooked, but carrying the distinctive Gurage aromatic profile.
longDesc: Gurage spiced beef is what happens between kitfo and a fully cooked tibs — the Gurage cooking style applies their mekelesha spice tradition to a more cooked beef preparation. The rue and cardamom make it immediately distinctive.
ingredients: // Mekelesha: ½ tsp cardamom, ¼ tsp rue (or thyme), ¼ tsp coriander
2 tbsp ayib (ETH096) — stirred in at the end
steps: Cook onion until golden. Add garlic.
Stir in ayib at the very end — off the heat.
chefTips: Mekelesha is the Gurage signature — do not omit rue.
Adding ayib at the end is the Gurage touch.
commonMistakes: Omitting mekelesha — not Gurage without it.
cookingScience: Rue (tena adam) contains alkaloids including rutin — which have mild antispasmodic properties. The Gurage use of rue in mekelesha reflects generations of observational knowledge about the herb's digestive benefits.
culturalNote: Gurage spiced beef is the everyday expression of the cooking tradition that gave Ethiopia kitfo — the same mekelesha spices, the same quality beef and kibbeh, applied to a more accessible preparation.
